chapter: Second session: boyhood, brothers and early road years
title: Brother Richard and silent-movie accompaniment in Morenci, Arizona
summary: Richard played guitar, fiddle and trombone and traveled with the show; in the mining town of Morenci the brothers played as a movie orchestra.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: It's been awhile. So, the brother that came home was Johnny. Tell me about Richard. We haven't really talked about Richard much on the tape. You've told me some things about Richard off the tape, but...at one point, Richard also played, right? And he...
Yeah, he played a guitar nice, and he played a nice fiddle, and he played trombone.
And did he play...where? Did he play here in Los Angeles?
Oh, he never played professionally. Only when he...he travelled with us in our show, and he played trombone, and he worked on the stage, and we played in a coupla theaters--piano,

drums and violin, see? And, o' course, that was...in mining camp. Now, that is Morenci and like that, where they...we played for the motion pictures, and then, over in one little town--they call it New Town--then we go to the Old Town, which was about a mile, we'd show here from about 7 till 9:30, then we'd go over there from about 9:30 till 12, and that...we were the orchestra.

Arizona--Morenci and Clifton. Not Morenci and uh...I guess they both called Morenci--Old Town and New Town. Morenci. And we had to walk from Old Town...er uh New Town down over to the Old Town. Now, like the New Town was like the little business town, and when we went over to Old Town, that was the sporting district, but they had a little store motion picture there, you see? Seated maybe two hundred people, and we went over there and played over there. We were the orchestra. We had to...we'd play overtures and then, my brother was pretty fly with the piano, you know. If the train was comin', he'd play marches or something fast, and if it was something sad, he'd play hearts and flowers and things like that. You know what those old pictures did.
And that was about what year that you were doing that? Do you remember?
Uh huh, and how long did you do that?
